question:
A 81-year-old man presents to clinic with his daughter for routine follow-up. He has no complaints, but
his daughter notes that he has recently become more fatigued with exertion and is sleeping more
frequently. He completed a 10-day course of ciprofloxacin last week for a prostate infection, and his
urinary symptoms have completely resolved. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes,
paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and moderate vascular dementia. His current medications include
donepezil 10 mg daily, verapamil 180 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, sotalol 120 mg twice daily, and
apixaban 5 mg twice daily. On physical examination, his temperature is 37.2°C, his blood pressure is
136/72 mm Hg, his heart rate is 45 beats per minute, and his respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute.
His lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination reveals a regular rhythm with no murmurs.
Jugular venous pressure is normal. Mild pitting edema is evident in both of his lower extremities. Which

one of the following next steps is most appropriate for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Reduce the
sotalol dose by 50% (B) Obtain an electrocardiogram (C) Check serum digoxin level (D) Initiate
temporary pacing (E) Order an echocardiogram (F) Schedule Holter monitoring (G) Obtain cardiac
biomarkers (H) Check serum electrolytes (I) Stop the verapamil with close follow-up (J) Obtain thyroid
function tests
 A. Schedule Holter monitoring
B. Obtain cardiac biomarkers
C. Check serum digoxin level
D. Reduce the sotalol dose by 50%
E. Check serum electrolytes
F. Stop the verapamil with close follow-up
G. Initiate temporary pacing
H. Obtain an electrocardiogram
I. Obtain thyroid function tests
J. Order an echocardiogram
